I tracked this down and pushed a fix in `f490f1ab`.

The issue was that encoder disconnect faults come through as `[MSG:ERR: ...]`, which were not part of the previous auto-save trigger path. The update now treats `[MSG:ERR: ...]` as a fault trigger and performs the serial auto-save on first fault capture, matching the one-save guard behavior.

@MaslowBot There is a restriction preventing Maslow from requesting a file write on browser for security reasons.
So, instead save an error log to the local file system on the Maslow containing the error information accessible via the FluidNC pulldown Local File System button.
Create file if it does not exist and append any error information.

> User @IDAbbott mentioned @MaslowBot with the following request:...

Implemented in `eca9ac0`.

Fault entries are now persisted on-device to LocalFS as `maslow-error.log`: each `[MSG:ERR: ...]` and `ALARM:...` line is appended (file is created automatically if missing). This makes the error history available via the FluidNC Local File System browser without relying on browser download prompts.

@BarbourSmith Saves Serial log automatically when 1st error encountered in a session. Preserves fault information for later analysis. Let me know what you think. 
Will save file to all sessions which have an open connection to the Maslow. This may cause duplicate log files.
That is a cool idea! So it will automatically download?

Yes, tested it by pulling the encoder plug, errored out and it downloaded the serial log. After restoring and resetting alarm get message saying position data may not be accurate etc. Subsequent pulling the encoder plug fault did not cause serial log dump, until after browser was refreshed, which reset the guard. Recommend implementing.
